doom.driver: The Cybersecurity Apocalypse Is Coming in 'Months,' AI Giants Warn. Plus: Hackers target over 100 US water systems, ICE puts in an order for robot dogs, and you'll never guess what "MrChildPorn" was arrested for.
doom.blurb: AI WARNS OF ITS OWN APOCALYPSE. HELPFUL.
doom.summary: The AI companies building the tools that could end civilization have generously warned us the cybersecurity apocalypse is just months away — which is either admirably transparent or the world's most sophisticated liability waiver. Meanwhile, hackers have already targeted over 100 US water systems, suggesting the apocalypse may be running slightly ahead of schedule. Berlin is also being ransomed by hackers today, so apparently 'months' was optimistic.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: SpaceX's acquisition of Cursor and AI giants issuing apocalyptic cybersecurity timelines in the same news cycle suggests the capability-governance gap is widening at an uncomfortable pace.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: EPA quietly letting data centers sidestep pollution laws signals continued regulatory capture by tech interests, with oversight infrastructure hollowing out.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: Trump's Venezuela oil deal granting US 'majority control' of 65 billion barrels is either a masterstroke or a geopolitical grenade with a very long fuse — Russia and China will have opinions.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: No major new alignment incidents today, but AI firms warning of imminent cyber catastrophe while simultaneously deploying more capable systems is its own form of misalignment.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: At least 37 killed in a Russian strike on Kyiv and 2,478 still missing in Nepal-Tibet floods — humanitarian crises mounting but neither represents a novel escalation vector today.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing — interior scene, we are inside a municipal water utility worker's break room in a mid-Atlantic American treatment plant, looking out through a single smudged window into the pre-dawn facility yard, deep navy and smoldering orange palette, smoke-filtered light, heavy shadows dominating — frost clings to the chain-link fence visible through the glass, concrete holding tanks loom in the murk beyond, but the tension is entirely inside the room: a folding table holds an open laptop showing a dark-mode Discord interface with a flagged username visible in the sidebar, beside it a stack of printed pages topped with a black asterisk OpenAI logo, the overhead fluorescent tube flickers casting sickly orange-tinged shadows across aged linoleum tile, on the far wall an Allen-Bradley PLC panel with blinking amber and red status LEDs mounted on a gray metal cabinet, pipes running floor to ceiling disappearing into the ceiling darkness, and through the window in the distant yard an ICE white SUV with green stripe sits idling, exhaust vapor rising in the cold air, headlights cutting through frost-misted darkness toward the facility gate where a Boston Dynamics Spot quadruped robot stands motionless on the concrete apron, its sensor head angled toward the building, alien and clinical, the whole scene suffused with the sense of multiple invisible systems converging on one ordinary room.

dawn.driver: Experimental eye drops help blind mice see again. Scientists have created light-activated drugs that helped blind mice perceive light again and restored visually guided behavior without gene therapy, implants, or specialized lighting.
dawn.summary: In a week shadowed by floods, strikes on Kyiv, and geopolitical brinkmanship, a quiet laboratory breakthrough cuts through the noise: scientists have restored light perception in blind mice using only eye drops. No implants, no gene therapy, no specialized equipment — just a drug that reactivates dormant photoreceptor pathways. The implications for human degenerative blindness conditions like retinitis pigmentosa are profound, pointing toward a future where vision loss may be chemically reversible rather than permanent.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: Light-activated eye drops restoring vision in blind mice represent a genuinely novel therapeutic mechanism that bypasses the complexity and cost of gene therapy entirely.

factors.name: Medicine
factors.detail: Researchers following 400,000 children for 20 years confirmed lasting cognitive advantages from public pre-K, a rare long-horizon win for evidence-based education policy.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: Australian researchers discovered iron-rich red soil can naturally generate hydrogen, potentially unlocking a vast clean energy source hiding in plain geological sight.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: A charity's 96 bridges across Rwanda's gorges and rivers showed measurable, life-changing impact on isolated communities — a study in how modest infrastructure reshapes human possibility.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Scientists identified a protein brake blocking nerve regeneration — blocking AHR allowed injured fibers to regrow — opening a credible new path toward treating spinal and peripheral nerve damage.

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. Wide aerial view looking down at a 45-degree angle, vast scene dominates the frame, tiny figures below. A sprawling low-vision rehabilitation center courtyard at golden hour, seen from high above, amber light raking long shadows across the grounds — the second-order world that vision restoration rewrites. The courtyard is full of life that was recently impossible: a tiny figure navigating a winding garden path without a white cane, arms loose at their sides; another small silhouette seated on a bench, face tilted upward toward the sky; a cluster of figures gathered around an outdoor reading board, leaning close. Wide garden beds run in long geometric strips, teal-shadowed between warm golden walkways. A low building edge frames the upper corner, its windows catching deep amber reflections. Long shadow fingers stretch dramatically across terracotta tiles. The color palette is deep golden hour amber and warm teal — the light of ordinary Tuesday afternoons, unremarkable and miraculous, the exact light that the new drops work in. Everything glows with radiant side-lighting, tiny human silhouettes casting long shadows, the whole vast courtyard humming with quiet motion that speaks of restored sight, not the laboratory that made it possible.
